subject: Scope & SLA: ephemeral retention during SSO migration
messages:
From: Clara Souza <clara@medsync.io>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medsync.io, procurement@medsync.io
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Temporary retention exception during SSO cutover

Hi Irene,

Quick note from MedSync: we have an SSO migration scheduled the week of Nov 22 and have one migration pattern that will create a brief spike in sign-in logs and webhook activity. Our security team is asking for a short-term retention exception so we can retain more detailed auth events (full headers + device IDs) for 14 days instead of the default ephemeral window. This is to support rollback diagnostics if the cutover produces unexpected token reuse in downstream connectors.

What we need from Redwood:
- Confirmation of whether a temporary retention window (14 days) is feasible without a formal BYOK exception.
- Any constraints on storing full-netflow/auth headers vs. hashed identifiers.
- A list of required evidence we need to provide to get approval (attestation, SOC snapshot, mitigation plan).

We can share the migration runbook and a minimal evidence pack — attaching our high-level flow. Can you advise next steps and who from Redwood we should loop in?

Thanks,
Clara Souza
Security Program Manager, MedSync
attachments: medsync_sso_flow.pdf
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Clara Souza <clara@medsync.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention exception during SSO cutover

Hi Clara — thanks for the heads up and the runbook.

Short answer: we can support a scoped, timeboxed retention increase for diagnostic events but we need to triage the exact fields you want to persist and confirm operational impact. Ben (security) and Marissa (product) are looped in to scope the ask; Grace will help with evidence requirements.

Initial questions for triage:
- Exact event types and fields (if you can call out the event names in the runbook that helps)
- Whether exported logs will be kept external to Redwood after the window
- Which tenants/environments are affected (staging vs prod)
- The justification and rollback criteria for the 14-day window

Can you drop a short matrix in reply (or to the retention_matrix.xlsx format) and we'll run an impact assessment and a proposed operational SLA for the exception.

Irene Choi
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention exception during SSO cutover

Irene — quick tech triage notes after looking at the runbook:

1) Feasibility: We can enable a 14-day diagnostic retention for auth events, limited to a specific tenant ID(s). It will be an opt-in config on the ingestion route and will be reversible.

2) Performance/Cost: Expect a ~12–18% increase in storage IO during the window depending on volume; for spikes we can route to a short-term hot tier. Estimate: $600–$1,200 for the two-week window (will compute more precisely with actual event volume).

3) Sensitive fields: We strongly recommend hashing device IDs and IPs while storing full headers only for request IDs and timestamps. Storing raw headers increases scope for data residency and potential PII handling. If MedSync insists on raw headers, we will need a signed exception and a temporary KMS key policy change.

4) BYOK: Not required for a timeboxed internal exception, but if MedSync wants exclusive key control for these logs we need BYOK + KMS integration (lead time ~3 weeks) and an updated KMS rotation policy.

5) Ops SLA: Proposed: 14 days retention enabled between Nov 22–Dec 6; Redwood will provide a retention-exception attestation and a downloadable evidence bundle (audit snapshot, access log) within 48 hours of request. We will restrict access to the MedSync security principal and Redwood on-call for the window.

I'll prepare a short proposal (attachment) with cost estimates and a minimal field-level mask plan.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: ephemeral_retention_proposal_v1.docx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention exception during SSO cutover

Thanks Ben — this looks reasonable. A few product/roadmap notes:

- Impact to product: If we implement as an ingestion-level flag + hot-tier routing, we can ship this as a short-lived 'incident-mode' feature without a product UI change. That keeps scope small (engineering effort: ~3 dev-days + 1 ops-day to validate).
- Prioritization: I can slot this as high priority for the week of Nov 15 to ensure config is ready before the cutover. We should avoid rolling BYOK changes if possible.
- Customer communication: Recommend a short ATO-style attestation email template that Grace can sign off on.

Open question for IR: do we require a formal change record for the exception or will an attestation + DocuSign signature suffice? If the latter, we can close the loop faster.

Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Clara Souza <clara@medsync.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retention exception during SSO cutover

Hi Clara — wrapping up next steps and approvals.

Summary of agreed plan:
- Scope: enable tenant-scoped diagnostic retention (auth events) for MedSync prod tenant only, 2026-11-22T00:00 to 2026-12-06T23:59 (14 days). Fields: request_id, timestamp, event_type, hashed_device_id, hashed_ip. Full headers will NOT be retained.
- Access: limited to MedSync security principal + Redwood on-call; audit exported at 48-hour cadence during the window.
- Evidence: Grace will deliver an attestation pack (SOC snapshot, access control matrix) and we will send a DocuSign acceptance for the exception.
- Cost: provisional estimate $900 for storage tiering during the window; final invoice will follow.

Attachments: retention_matrix.xlsx (please review fields mapping), ephemeral_retention_proposal_v1.docx, medsync_sso_flow.pdf
DocuSign acceptance: https://docusign.com/some-ds-link/medsync-exception

If that matches MedSync's needs, Clara please sign the DocuSign and reply with the confirmed tenant ID and the exact list of event names you want preserved. We'll turn the config on the 22nd and send the first audit snapshot within 48 hours.

Thanks — appreciate the cooperation here.

Irene Choi
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
